references.text: Joseph explains to his brothers that it was God who sent him ahead of them to Egypt and made him ruler over all Pharaoh's house, showing God's plan behind his elevation.
The Lord was with Joseph and gave him success in everything he did in Potiphar's house, foreshadowing his later rise to rule over all Egypt.
The psalm describes how Pharaoh set Joseph as ruler over his household and as governor over all his possessions—a direct reference to his elevation in Genesis 41:41.
Stephen recounts in his speech how God gave Joseph favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, who appointed him to govern Egypt and all his household.
Daniel is elevated by Nebuchadnezzar to rule over the entire province of Babylon after interpreting the king's dream, a strong parallel to Joseph's elevation following dream interpretation.
Pharaoh's human appointment is confirmed as a divine arrangement through Joseph's own interpretation.
The verses show the connection between the theoretical authority given to Joseph and its practical application during the crisis.
The New Testament confirms that Pharaoh's appointment of Joseph was part of God's plan to display His power.
A clear contrast between Pharaoh's elevation to save Israel and his later judgment over that same power.
